notes.text:
Week
01

API basics
Lesson 1
What an API is
An API is a menu of requests a program accepts.
The client asks, the server answers.
Cheat sheet:
Client = asks
Server = answers
Endpoint = one address on the menu

notes.title: Routes and status codes
notes.text:
Lesson 2
Routes and status codes
A route connects a URL to a function.
200 OK, 201 Created, 404 Not Found.
For finals:
Know which code goes with which result.
notes.refined:
IN PLAIN WORDS
A route connects a URL to a function, and every answer has a status code: 200 OK, 201 Created, 404 Not Found.

————— YOUR NOTES (tidied) —————

A route connects a URL to a function:
```python
@app.get("/hello")
def hello():
    return {"msg": "hi"}, 200
```
For finals:
Know which code goes with which result.
200 = OK, 201 = Created, 404 = Not Found

notes.title: Hashing passwords
notes.text:
Week
02
Jan 12 - Jan 19
Real users
Lesson 1
Hashing passwords
Never store the password. Store a hash.
The default method is pbkdf2.
Key exam idea:
Hashing is one-way; you can only check a guess.
notes.refined:
IN PLAIN WORDS
Never store a password, only a one-way hash. Login re-hashes the guess and compares.

————— YOUR NOTES (tidied) —————

Never store the password. Store a hash.
```python
from werkzeug.security import generate_password_hash, check_password_hash
h = generate_password_hash("secret")
check_password_hash(h, "secret")  # True
```
Key exam idea:
Hashing is one-way; you can only check a guess.

CORRECTION (checked by running it)
In current Werkzeug the default method is scrypt, not pbkdf2. check_password_hash reads the method from the hash, so both still work.

MORE EXACT (game fact)
This demo has no real game facts; this block only tests that game-fact fixes stay out of Final prep.

notes.title: Tokens and 401 vs 403
notes.text:
Lesson 2
Tokens and 401 vs 403
401 = we don't know who you are.
403 = we know you, but you can't do this.
Memorize:
missing or bad token → 401
not allowed → 403
notes.refined:
IN PLAIN WORDS
401 means the server can't tell who you are; 403 means it knows you but you're not allowed.

————— YOUR NOTES (tidied) —————

401 = we don't know who you are.
403 = we know you, but you can't do this.
Memorize:
missing or bad token → 401
not allowed → 403
